question: Which river in Jammu and Kashmir has the world’s highest railway bridge built over it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir is home to the world's highest railway bridge, known as the **Chenab Bridge**.
 
• The Chenab Bridge is part of the **Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project** undertaken by the Indian Railways.
 
• It stands at a height of **359 meters (1,178 feet)** above the riverbed, making it taller than the Eiffel Tower.
 
• The bridge spans **1,315 meters** and is designed to withstand wind speeds up to 266 km/h and earthquakes of high intensity.
 
• Construction of the Chenab Bridge was completed in **2022**, marking a significant engineering achievement in challenging terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chenab River:** It originates from the Baralacha Pass in Himachal Pradesh and flows through Jammu and Kashmir before entering Pakistan.
 
• **USBRL Project:** This ambitious rail link aims to connect the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India, enhancing connectivity and boosting regional development.
 
• **Engineering Challenges:** The construction of the Chenab Bridge involved overcoming steep gorges, high-altitude conditions, and seismic challenges.
 
• **Steel Arch Design:** The bridge has a steel arch design, making it resilient against geological and climatic challenges in the Himalayan region.
 
• **Strategic Importance:** The bridge plays a crucial role in improving transportation and economic integration in Jammu and Kashmir.
